laat_vaar.blok: Wat die kaart van jou provinsie vertel
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Volg die lyn rond' echoes English 'follow the line around'; 'al om' is the natural Afrikaans for going all the way round.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Volg die lyn rond' is understandable Afrikaans, while 'al om' without an object ('al om die provinsie') reads incomplete, so the proposal is not clearly better.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoe jy dit self in die atlas doen
laat_vaar.na: Lees die kaart met die sleutel
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two maps are named just before, so 'dit' is vague; naming the map makes the reference clear without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Both maps just named are 'kaart', so 'die kaart' is no less ambiguous than 'dit' and adds a third 'kaart' in three sentences; the original 'dit' fittingly covers whichever map the learner has.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat die kaart van jou provinsie vertel
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Hom' for a province reads informally and the referent is clearer when named.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Hom' for a province is normal Afrikaans and here can only point to the province, so naming it again is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoe jy dit self in die atlas doen
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Kry' in the sense of 'find' is colloquial; 'soek' is the standard instruction.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Kry' (find) is standard Afrikaans here, while 'soek' (search) changes the action and repeats 'soek' from the next sentence.
